Why cancelled?? I cannot add Minecraft integration because I'm running Minecraft in Docker, and using IP address is far more reliable than MAC address lookup.

@firestrife23 Cancelled because the HASS team refuse to accept the changes. Take a look at the fork of this integration at https://github.com/cyberjacob/minecraft-home-assistant/ which includes the changes.

> Why cancelled?? I cannot add Minecraft integration because I'm running Minecraft in Docker, and using IP address is far more reliable than MAC address lookup.

Using IP address for an unique ID is just wrong and should not be done. It will cause problems in the long run. Instead, don't use a unique ID or use the one provided by the config entry.

> Cancelled because the HASS team refuse to accept the changes.

That is incorrect, the PR was closed because the PR author hasn't implemented the needed requirements and left it running stale.

> Using IP address for an unique ID is just wrong and should not be done. It will cause problems in the long run. Instead, don't use a unique ID or use the one provided by the config entry.

While that may be true for some people, however, my servers are assigned with static IP. Thank you for clarification, and I will use @cyberjacob's fork in the meantime.

Hmm... Could you try your hostname with the ending `.local` (`hostname.local`)? Maybe it's also different on your side, this depends on your router. With my AVM router it's for example `hostname.fritz.box`.

Did anyone find a solution for this? I am still unable to add my minecraft server due to the same issues (IP address is invalid (MAC address could not be determined). Please correct it and try again.) Is there no workaround to disable the MAC address validation?

review_comments: What kind of host address is this? Could it change?
The host is specified in the configuration, it may be an IPv4/IPv6 address or a DNS name. For example: `minecraft.example.com` or `1.1.1.1`.
We normally don't allow IP addresses as unique id as they may change for the same device or service.

@cyberjacob That is why in the initial PR for the integration I used the MAC address as the unique ID in case of IP addresses (with the limitation that it doesn't work if the MAC address is not readable). Actually this was a review finding by @MartinHjelmare back then. 

Counter-proposal: Instead, a second step in the config flow could be added for manual entry of the MAC address, if it's not readable...

If your argument is that the IP address may change, the same could happen for a MAC address. And that a different IP could easily be considered a different server. MAC addresses are also shared between different IPs on a single host, causing a possibility for conflicts.

I'd also point out that for the identifier to change, the server would have to be manually removed and re-added by the user. Servers accessed via a DNS record (weather A, AAAA, or SRV) use this record as part of the identifier (this functionality has not changed).
Ok, do you have an alternate suggestion for fixing this bug?
As I said before: One solution would be to ask the user for the MAC address, in case it can‘t be read. This can be probably done with a 2nd step in the config flow.

> We normally don't allow IP addresses as unique id as they may change for the same device or service.

If the case that the IP address changes the integration would have to be removed and set up again anyway since the Minecraft server would no longer exist on the IP address that Home Assistant would be querying anyway - Because of this I can't see any problem with using the IP address as the entity id? Failing that being allowed I can't see any other attribute that could be the unique ID, aside from the MAC address - which breaks under reasons given above.

Surely a MAC address isn't really a unique ID? If I'm running more than one minecraft server on the same host, or using a shared hosting platform with multiple servers per host then more than one minecraft server could share the same MAC address. In this instance, an IP:Port combination would be preferred, as it's generally not possible to run multiple services on the same port on a host. 

Additionally, generally servers have static IP assignments and thus the IP address will be unlikely to change without specific user intervention and even if the IP did change, the integration would have to be reconfigured anyway as it connects to an IP and port in order to read data from the minecraft instance.

Good point. We should remove mac address too.

Use config entry ID.
